title: macOS (Apple Silicon) support: native build running under Rosetta 2 with MoltenVK
body:
## Overview

This adds a native macOS build target for Apple Silicon. The emulator compiles and runs as an x86_64 binary under Rosetta 2 (guest PS5 code executes natively as x86_64; the emulator itself is translated), with graphics going through Vulkan to MoltenVK to Metal. It builds on the current tree, boots a commercial title into gameplay, and responds to controller input.

## What was tested

Raiden III x MIKADO MANIAX boots through the loader, Vulkan init, swapchain, and window creation into guest execution, renders frames continuously, and takes controller input; the audio pipeline is wired up. It is a functional port with a couple of known rendering artifacts and performance still to improve (see Known issues), not a finished product, but well past proof of concept.

Verified locally on an M3 Pro MacBook Pro: clean configure, build, link, JIT codesign, and launch under Rosetta 2.

## Building on macOS

Prerequisites: Apple Silicon Mac, Rosetta 2, Xcode Command Line Tools, CMake, Ninja, and a Vulkan runtime that provides MoltenVK (for example the LunarG Vulkan SDK for macOS).

```sh
git clone --recursive https://github.com/<you>/KytyPS5
cd KytyPS5
cmake -S src -B _Build/macos -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64
cmake --build _Build/macos --target kyty_emulator --parallel
```

The build produces an x86_64 binary and codesigns it with the JIT entitlements automatically. Run a game with `--game <dir|elf>` (see `--help` for options). If the window fails to appear because of a Rosetta issue in the macOS window chrome, set `KYTY_BORDERLESS=1` for a borderless window.

## Known issues

- Some rendering artifacts remain: video noise during cutscenes and a black box around certain sprites. These are on the texture-upload side and under investigation; they do not block boot or input.
- Frame rate is modest (around 26 fps in the tested title). This appears consistent with the title's general performance and is not macOS-specific.
- The guest Ngs2 audio path uses a stub for one call, which may leave a gap in some in-game audio.

title: fix Windows fixed placeholder reservations below allocation granularity
body:
## What changed

- Fix Windows fixed placeholder reservations when a PS5 16 KiB mapping starts at an address that is not aligned to the Windows allocation granularity.
- Reserve the enclosing allocation-granularity placeholder container, split it, release the unused neighboring ranges, and retain an exact placeholder for the requested range.
- Add `FixedSub64KDirectMapUsesExactAddress`, covering fixed reservation, exact direct-memory mapping, shared-backing aliasing, unmap, placeholder restoration, and release of the neighboring host ranges.

## Why

UFC 5 fails early in #100 while mapping `EAOSGlobal` at `0xfbffffc000` with a size of `0x4000`.

`VirtualAlloc2` requires a non-null fixed base address to be aligned to the system allocation granularity. The affected address is a valid 16 KiB PS5-page address but is offset within a 64 KiB Windows allocation-granularity range.

The fix reserves an aligned placeholder container and uses placeholder splitting so that `MapViewOfFile3(..., MEM_REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER)` receives a placeholder whose base address and size exactly match the requested mapping.

## Documentation

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/memoryapi/nf-memoryapi-virtualalloc2
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/memoryapi/nf-memoryapi-mapviewoffile3
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/memoryapi/nf-memoryapi-virtualfree

## Validation

- Built on Windows with the project CMake/Ninja configuration:
  `cmake --build Build\windows --target kyty_emulator virtual_memory_allocation_tests`
- Ran `virtual_memory_allocation_tests`: 27/27 cases passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Ran clang-format validation for `src/kernel/memoryAddressSpace.inc`.
- Reproduced UFC 5 (`PPSA03541`): the original `placeholder-reserve-failed` / fatal error no longer occurs. `EAOSGlobal` now maps at `0xfbffffc000` with `shared = yes`.

## Scope

This partially addresses #100. The new UFC 5 log proceeds far beyond the original memory failure but later stops on an unrelated `unsupported storage texture` renderer error, so this PR should not close #100.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation support, test design, and documentation research. I have reviewed the final diff and validation results and remain responsible for this contribution.

title: MacOS (Apple Silicon) native support - any interest?
body:
## Summary
The listed platforms in the README.md don't include macOS, so I built a native macOS (Apple Silicon) port on top of the current codebase and have it running real content.

Inititally it was only meant for my own personal use so that I could game on my Mac, but I believe there's genuine value in upstreaming this. But before I start cleaning it up, I wanted to confirm that there's KytyPS5's interest in upstreaming this support.


## Approach
- Builds and runs natively on macOS/arm64 by targeting x86_64 under Rosetta 2.
- Graphics go through Vulkan → MoltenVK → Metal.
- Required changes so far: CMake/toolchain adjustments, a set of first-compile portability fixes, shm_open/page-fault-handler porting, and a handful of address-space and inline-asm corrections for the Rosetta environment.

## I've tested this with
- MOSS Raiden III x MIKADO MANIAX

It works with a few known rendering artifacts and perf work still in progress (I'm getting low FPS atm), not finished at the moment but still past the proof-of-concept stage.

Open to thoughts and comments.

title: cleanup: drop unused n_frames, suppress C4996 for codecvt use site
body:
﻿## Root cause

Two small cleanups in kyty code (3rdparty/tracy warnings are out of scope).

1. src/graphics/presentation/window/window.cpp:1168 had a static uint32_t n_frames that was incremented and reset inside ShowFps(), but the printf in the same block uses m_frame_num (the engine's own counter) — not 
_frames. So the local counter was set but never read; clang's -Wunused-but-set-variable flagged it.

2. src/common/stringUtils.h:321 uses std::wstring_convert<std::codecvt_utf8_utf16<char16_t>, char16_t>, which MSVC deprecates with C4996. The stdlib's _SILENCE_CXX17_CODECVT_HEADER_DEPRECATION_WARNING macro is checked by the implementation *before* the <codecvt> include, so a top-of-header #define is too late. Wrapping the use site in #pragma warning(push/disable/pop) is the standard fix and kyty already uses the same pattern elsewhere.

## Files

- src/common/stringUtils.h — 1 use site, 5 lines added (comment + pragma push/disable/pop)
- src/graphics/presentation/window/window.cpp — 3 lines removed (the 
_frames decl, increment, and reset)

Total: 2 files, +9 / -4, no functional change.

## Verification

Build before: 18 kyty warnings (16 codecvt deprecations, 1 unused-but-set, 1 from #include-vs-#define ordering).

Build after: 0 kyty warnings (3rdparty/tracy's 4 warnings untouched).

V24 sweep (30 ELFs, 15s timeout) after this commit:
- 30/30 M1W2 v1.3 patch fires
- 28/30 Vulkan robustness (V23 was 29/30; difference is non-determinism — V23's sdk_ver reached Vulkan, V24's hwinfo didn't. Both run near the gate. V24's sdk_ver did reach Vulkan init this time.)
- 0 fatal / 0 fail-fast

No behavioral change.

## AI-assisted disclosure

Developed with AI assistance (Claude/oh-my-claudecode). All edits and verification done locally with the user's 30-ELF test corpus.

title: [GAME BUG]: EA Sports College Football 25 (stuck in infinite loop, never reaches menu)
body: ### Game title EA Sports College Football 25 ### Game ID / serial PPSA04184 ### KytyPS5 version 0.2.2 ### Last working build / first broken build _No response_ ### What happened? **Current Blocker - unimplemented `libkernel` import causes an infinite wait** The game does not reach the main menu. Over the course of investigating this, three distinct emulator bugs were found and fixed, after which the game now hangs indefinitely in a busy-loop on an unimplemented `libkernel` import. The game boots further: it loads `eboot.bin` and several `.prx` modules, sets up its EA engine memory pools, and creates an `EAThread Timer Queue`. It then enters what looks like a queue/free-list processing loop and calls an **unresolved `libkernel_v1.1` import** (encoded NID `lgK+oIWkJyA`) once per iteration. Because that function isn't implemented, it unconditionally returns `0`; the game's code appears to treat that as "not ready, check again" and spins forever, so it never falls through to whatever comes after this step in its boot sequence (and the menu never appears). There were some other issues that i fixed on my own. to get to this point. Detailed here: **Bug 1 — Vulkan device-layer validation error (fixed)** `vkCreateDevice()` was being called with `enabledLayerCount = 1`, enabling `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` at the *device* level. Device-level layers have been non-functional since Vulkan 1.0 and current validation layers hard-reject a non-zero `enabledLayerCount` on `VkDeviceCreateInfo`. This crashed immediately on launch. - File: `src/graphics/presentation/window/vulkanWindow.cpp` (~line 672) - Fix: zero `enabledLayerCount`/`ppEnabledLayerNames` on the device create info; the instance already enables the validation layer correctly elsewhere in the same file. **Bug 2 — Windows 64KB allocation-granularity vs PS5 16KB page granularity (fixed)** After Bug 1 was fixed, the game crashed again shortly after loading, with an access violation writing to address `0x18` inside `eboot.bin`. Root cause: the game's engine (EA's "EAOSGlobal" allocator) requests fixed-address direct-memory mappings at addresses aligned to the PS5's native 16KB page size, but **not** to Windows' 64KB `VirtualAlloc` allocation granularity. `MapPlaceholderView()` tried to reserve a fresh placeholder at the *exact* requested address via `VirtualAlloc2(..., MEM_RESERVE_PLACEHOLDER, ...)`, which Windows can never satisfy unless the base address is 64KB-aligned — regardless of whether the address is actually free. Every candidate address the engine tried failed identically, its allocator init silently produced a null object, and the game later wrote through that null pointer. - File: `src/kernel/memoryAddressSpace.inc`, `DirectMemoryBacking::MapPlaceholderView()` - Fix: when the requested range isn't itself granularity-aligned, reserve (or reuse) the containing 64KB-aligned block first, then split it down to the exact requested sub-range using the same preserve-placeholder split technique already used elsewhere in the file (see `UnmapOne`). **Bug 3 — `sceKernelQueryMemoryProtection` crashed on a null guest pointer (fixed)** A secondary hardening fix: this function used `EXIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED(addr == nullptr)`, crashing the whole emulator when a guest-supplied pointer was null, instead of returning `KERNEL_ERROR_EFAULT` like every comparable function in the same file. Real PS5 hardware returns an error for a bad pointer argument here; it doesn't crash the console. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open KytyPS5. 2. Boot EA Sports College Football 25 (PPSA04184). 3. Observe the emulator initializes subsystems, loads modules, and then never proceeds — log fills with repeated `Unresolved import stub called: lgK+oIWkJyA[libkernel_v1][libkernel_v1.1][Func]`. ### Expected behavior Splash screens should render, followed by the main menu. ### OS Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 ### CPU AMD Ryzen 9 9900X ### GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 ### RAM / VRAM 32 GB RAM / 12 GB VRAM ### Log file upload [_kyty.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30169273/_kyty.txt) ### Screenshots/video ### Extra notes _No response_

title: PS5 ELF loader: handle DT_REL (legacy) relocation format
body:
﻿# PS5 ELF loader: handle DT_REL (legacy) relocation format

## Summary

Kyty's ELF dynamic loader only accepted `DT_RELA` (relocation entries with
explicit addends). Every PS5 SDK homebrew ELF (e.g. elfldr, ftpsrv, gdbsrv,
klogsrv, shsrv, websrv from issue #33) ships `DT_REL` instead, so the loader
crashed at `runtimeLinker.cpp:2120` with `Not implemented (true)` before the
guest program could ever start. This PR teaches the loader to expand
`DT_REL` records into `DT_RELA` in-place, matching glibc `ld.so`'s behaviour.

## Root cause

`ParseProgramDynamicInfo` had three hard-coded exit points for ELFs that
were not DT_RELA-only:

1. `EXIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED(jmprel_type != DT_RELA)` â€” bailed on any
   `DT_PLTREL` value other than 7.
2. `EXIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED(!is_shared && !is_next_gen)` â€” refused to load
   any non-shared ELF whose abiversion was <2 (i.e. every legacy SDK ELF).
3. `EXIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED(program->dynamic_info->jmprela_table == nullptr)`
   in `RelocateProgram` â€” even after the table was correctly populated,
   this assertion ran *before* the call, so an empty PLT (legitimate
   for ELFs without `.plt`) aborted the load.

## Fix

Three small, surgical changes in `src/loader/`:

1. **runtimeLinker.cpp**: introduce a local `Elf64_Rel` mirror struct and a
   `UpgradeRelToRela(rel_addr, rel_sz)` helper. For each `Elf64_Rel` record
   we allocate a fresh `Elf64_Rela`, copy `r_offset` / `r_info`, and resolve
   the implicit addend by reading the current 64-bit value at the target
   address. This is exactly what glibc `ld.so` does in `elf/dl-reloc.c`
   `elf_dynamic_do_rel()` for ELF64.

   The PLT branch (`DT_PLTREL == DT_REL`) and the main relocation table
   branch both call the helper, then patch the corresponding `*_table_size`
   fields to match the new `Elf64_Rela` size (24 bytes) instead of
   `Elf64_Rel` (16 bytes). A new `jmprel_type == 0` case handles ELFs with
   no `.plt` (e.g. self-contained loader ELFs).

   The `RelocateProgram` function now skips the PLT pass when
   `jmprela_table == nullptr`.

2. **elf.h**: define the missing `DT_RELENT` (0x12) and `DT_OS_RELENT`
   (0x61000032) constants. Also fix the `GetDynamicData<T>` template â€”
   it returned `nullptr` in the "no data" branch, which is ill-formed for
   non-pointer `T` (e.g. `uint64_t`). Replaced with `T{}` which yields a
   properly zero-initialised value for any `T`.

3. **elf.cpp / elf.h** (from a prior loader-fix pass): accept standard
   `ET_DYN` (3) in addition to the Sony-specific `ET_DYNEXEC` / `ET_DYNAMIC`
   types. PS5 SDK ELFs ship as `ET_DYN` so this is required just to reach
   the relocation parser.

## Evidence

Smoke tests against the 6 PS5 SDK test ELFs from issue #33, with the fix
applied:

| ELF        | Before fix                          | After fix                                           |
|------------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| elfldr.elf | `Not implemented (true)` at line 2060 (DT_REL) | Reaches "Relocate program", runs entry, fails on missing DirectMemory backing (CreateFileMapping 0x5AA â€” separate Windows-memory subsystem issue) |
| ftpsrv.elf | `Not implemented (true)` at line 2060 | Reaches "Relocate program", runs entry, hits `Access violation: Execute [0x1]` â€” i.e. jumps to a NULL stub (loader-level issue fully cleared) |
| gdbsrv.elf | `Not implemented (true)` at line 2060 | Same as ftpsrv                                      |
| klogsrv.elf | DT_REL blocker                      | Passes DT_REL, fails on next loader gate            |
| shsrv.elf  | DT_REL blocker                      | Passes DT_REL, fails on next loader gate            |
| websrv.elf | DT_REL blocker                      | Passes DT_REL, fails on next loader gate            |

All six ELFs are now past the DT_REL gate. The remaining failures are
unrelated loader-gate or Windows-memory issues, out of scope for this PR.

## Out of scope / future work

- The `EXIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED(rel_entsz != 0 && rel_entsz != sizeof(Elf64_Rel))`
  check is a guard rail: an ELF that advertises a non-zero DT_RELENT but
  with a value different from 16 bytes will still abort. In practice every
  ABI-compliant toolchain writes 16; we can soften this later if a real ELF
  ever trips it.
- Memory backing failure (`CreateFileMapping 0x5AA`) is a separate,
  pre-existing issue in `DirectMemoryBacking::SelfTest`. Will be addressed
  in its own PR.

## AI-assisted disclosure

This PR was authored with significant AI assistance (Claude / MiniMax-M3)
working from a user-supplied goal ("make one perfect PR, that realy
improve"). All code paths were smoke-tested against six real PS5 SDK ELFs.

Closes / unblocks kyty issue #33.

title: Improve Windows memory and Intel Vulkan compatibility
body:
This PR fixes a couple of issues that prevented some games from starting on Windows, especially on systems using Intel integrated graphics.
Direct memory is now committed only when needed instead of reserving everything at startup, vulkan can also reuse a single universal queue when the GPU does not expose separate queues.
I also removed a storage image feature requirement that the emulator wasn’t actually using.
With these changes, Dreaming Sarah now boots and renders correctly on Intel Iris Xe graphics.

title: cmake: preserve spaces in clang-cl linker paths
body:
## Summary

Pass linker flags as individual CMake options so PDB and linker map paths remain intact when the build directory contains spaces.

The existing `LINK_FLAGS` string splits these paths before the final link. This change uses `target_link_options` so CMake passes each option correctly.

## Testing

The failure reproduced in two clean Release configurations. The fixed branch completed a Release build in a path containing spaces, installation succeeded, the launcher started correctly, and all ten existing test executables passed.

## AI disclosure

I used AI to help investigate the failure, prepare the change, and run the verification commands. I reviewed the change, reproduction evidence, test results, and this pull request text before submission.

title: Build fails with Vulkan SDK 1.4.350: vk_enum_string_helper.h mismatches bundled Vulkan-Headers (v335)
body:
## Summary

  The README lists "Vulkan SDK 1.3 or newer" as a build requirement, but building
  with the current SDK (1.4.350.0) fails. The repo bundles Vulkan-Headers at
  header version 335 (`3rdparty/Vulkan-Headers`), which is first in the include
  path — but `vk_enum_string_helper.h` is not part of Vulkan-Headers (it ships
  with the SDK, from Vulkan-Utility-Libraries). So the ~14 sources that include
  it get the SDK 1.4.350 copy, which references enums that don't exist in the
  v335 `vulkan_core.h`.

  ## Error

  First failure is in `src/graphics/host_gpu/renderer/renderCompute.cpp`:

      C:\VulkanSDK\1.4.350.0\Include\vulkan/vk_enum_string_helper.h(1291,14):
      error: use of undeclared identifier
      'VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_FAULT_SHADER_ABORT_MESSAGE_INFO_KHR'

  followed by similar undeclared-identifier errors until the error limit.

  ## Steps to reproduce

  1. Install Vulkan SDK 1.4.350.0 (current latest)
  2. Configure and build per the README (clang-cl + Ninja, Windows)
  3. Compilation fails in every file that includes `<vulkan/vk_enum_string_helper.h>`

  ## Workaround

  Install Vulkan SDK **1.4.335.0**, which matches the bundled headers exactly —
  the build then succeeds.

  ## Suggested fixes

  Any of these would prevent the trap:
  - Document the supported/pinned SDK version in the README instead of "1.3 or newer"
  - Add a CMake configure-time check comparing the SDK's `VK_HEADER_VERSION`
    against the bundled Vulkan-Headers version, failing with a clear message
  - Vendor a matching `vk_enum_string_helper.h` so the SDK copy is never used

  I'm happy to submit a PR for whichever direction the maintainers prefer.

  ## Environment

  - Windows 11, VS 2022 Build Tools with clang-cl 19.1.5
  - CMake 4.4.0, Ninja 1.13.2, Qt 6.8.3
  - Repo at current `main` (f743a48), submodules at pinned revisions

  ## AI disclosure

  Per the project's AI-use policy: I used an AI tool (Claude Code) to help
  diagnose the header mismatch and identify the affected include chain. I
  personally reproduced the failure (clean build with Vulkan SDK 1.4.350.0),
  confirmed the exact error output above, and verified that installing SDK
  1.4.335.0 resolves it by completing a full build and running the emulator.
  This issue text was reviewed and edited by me.

title: Register regression tests with CTest
body:
## What changed

- Register the existing regression executables with CTest.
- Add a `kyty_tests` target that builds the complete regression suite.
- Document the build and test commands.
- Avoid an implementation-dependent UNORM8 rounding tie in the inverse-swizzle GPU tests by using an input with one valid nearest result.

## Why

The repository already had ten focused regression executables, but they had to be discovered and run manually. This makes the existing coverage available through the standard CMake/CTest workflow and keeps the GPU tests portable across Vulkan drivers.

## Validation

- Built the `kyty_tests` target on Windows with clang-cl.
- Ran `ctest --output-on-failure`: 10/10 tests passed.
- Ran `git diff --check`.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to inspect the test configuration, research the Vulkan UNORM conversion rule, and prepare the initial patch. The contributor reviewed the complete diff and confirmed it for submission. The full test suite was built and run locally before opening this pull request.
